title: HeroUI Frontend
moduleObjectives: Install Node.js with nvm and confirm `node`, `npm`, and `npx` resolve to nvm-managed paths
Initialize a HeroUI starter project with Next.js and Tailwind pre-configured and run its dev server with hot reload
Build interactive pages using HeroUI components such as `Button`, `Input`, `Card`, and `Checkbox`, applying the `"use client"` directive where hooks are used
Enable CORS in the FastAPI backend with `CORSMiddleware` so the browser-based frontend can call it
Fetch items from `http://localhost:8000/items` and render them as HeroUI Cards with loading, error, and empty states
Build a form that POSTs new items to the API and refreshes the displayed list inline without a page reload
Use Continue.dev chat, inline edit, and agent mode to extend the frontend, reviewing every proposed diff before accepting
Ship a frontend change through a branch, commit, and merge or GitHub PR workflow

lessons.title: Prerequisites Check
lessons.objective: Verify that the FastAPI Compose stack, Continue.dev connection, and GitHub remote from earlier modules still work and that no conflicting system Node.js installation is present.

lessons.title: Install Node.js with nvm
lessons.objective: Install nvm and the latest LTS release of Node.js, set it as the default, and confirm `node`, `npm`, and `npx` run from nvm-managed paths under your home directory.

lessons.title: Init the HeroUI App
lessons.objective: Scaffold a Next.js + HeroUI starter project with `npx heroui-cli@latest init`, install its dependencies, and run the dev server so the starter page loads on port 3000.

lessons.title: Tour + First Component
lessons.objective: Build an interactive homepage from HeroUI `Button`, `Card`, and `Input` components and explain when a Next.js page needs the `"use client"` directive to use React hooks.

lessons.title: CORS + Fetch Items
lessons.objective: Add `CORSMiddleware` to the FastAPI backend and fetch the items list from the browser, rendering each item as a HeroUI Card with loading, error, and empty states.

lessons.title: Create-Item Form
lessons.objective: Build a HeroUI form that POSTs new items to FastAPI, converts input strings to the types the API expects, surfaces server validation errors, and reloads the list inline on success.

lessons.title: Extend with Continue.dev
lessons.objective: Use Continue.dev agent mode on a git feature branch to add a Delete button with a confirmation modal, reviewing every proposed diff and recognizing when to abort a failing agent loop.

lessons.title: Final Checkpoint
lessons.objective: Ship a client-side, case-insensitive search filter for the items page end-to-end using Continue.dev, verify it in the browser, and commit and merge the change.

quiz.question: After a successful nvm installation, running `which nvm` prints nothing. Why is that expected?
options: The installation failed and must be re-run with sudo
nvm only becomes visible after you reboot the machine
nvm is a shell function sourced from `~/.bashrc`, not a binary, so you verify it with `command -v nvm`
The `which` command is not available in bash
quiz.feedback: nvm is loaded into the shell as a function from `~/.bashrc`, so `which` finds no binary; `command -v nvm` is the correct check.

quiz.question: Which command does the module use to scaffold the Next.js + HeroUI starter project?
options: `npx heroui-cli@latest init`
`npm install -g @heroui/react && heroui init`
`npx create-next-app --heroui`
`docker run heroui/starter`
quiz.feedback: The lesson runs the HeroUI CLI on the fly with npx, avoiding any global install, and answers its prompts to create the project.

quiz.question: You add `useState` to a page in the `app/` directory and the browser shows an error saying the hook only works in a Client Component. What is the fix taught in the module?
options: Restart the dev server with `npm run dev`
Move the hook into `app/layout.tsx`
Downgrade to an older version of Next.js
Add `"use client";` as the very first line of the file
quiz.feedback: Pages in `app/` default to server components, so any component using hooks must opt in with the `"use client"` directive at the top of the file.

quiz.question: Which prop do HeroUI's `Input` and `Checkbox` components use to hand you the new value directly, per the lessons?
options: `onChange`
`onValueChange`
`onInput`
`setValue`
quiz.feedback: HeroUI's idiomatic prop is `onValueChange`, which passes the value itself rather than a DOM event like `onChange` does.

quiz.question: The page at `http://localhost:3000` fails to fetch `http://localhost:8000/items` and the browser console says the request was blocked by CORS policy. What fixes this in the course setup?
options: Change the fetch call to use `mode: "no-cors"`
Serve the frontend from port 8000 instead
Add `CORSMiddleware` to the FastAPI app with `allow_origins=["http://localhost:3000"]`
Add an `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` header to the fetch request in React
quiz.feedback: CORS is granted by the server, so the fix is adding FastAPI's `CORSMiddleware` configured to allow the frontend's origin.

quiz.question: Why does `curl http://localhost:8000/items` succeed even while the browser fetch from the frontend is blocked by CORS?
options: CORS is enforced by browsers, so curl and server-side code are not affected
curl automatically includes the required Origin headers
The API whitelists curl's User-Agent by default
curl bypasses CORS by using HTTP/2
quiz.feedback: CORS is a browser security mechanism; tools like curl never enforce it, which is why the same endpoint works from the terminal.

quiz.question: In the create-item form, why does the submit handler send `Number(price)` instead of `price` in the POST body?
options: `Number()` validates that the price is positive
`JSON.stringify` cannot serialize strings
FastAPI would round string prices incorrectly
The Input's value is a string, and the API expects `price` as a number
quiz.feedback: Form input values are always strings, so the code converts the price to a number before sending it to match what the API expects.

quiz.question: After the form's POST succeeds, what must the handler do so the new item appears in the list without reloading the page?
options: Call `window.location.reload()`
Clear the form and re-fetch the items list, e.g. `await loadItems()`
Nothing — React re-renders automatically after any fetch
Restart the Next.js dev server
quiz.feedback: The lesson stresses re-fetching the list state after a successful POST; otherwise the new item only shows up on the next manual refresh.

quiz.question: Before letting Continue.dev's agent mode change the frontend, what does the module tell you to do first?
options: Create a git feature branch so a bad result is easy to revert
Delete `node_modules` so the agent runs faster
Stop the FastAPI backend so the agent cannot call it
Switch Continue.dev to autocomplete mode
quiz.feedback: The rule is branch first, agent second: working on a feature branch means junk output can be discarded with a simple revert.

quiz.question: How does the final checkpoint's search box filter the items list?
options: It calls a new FastAPI `/items/search` endpoint
It runs a SQL LIKE query through a new backend route
It filters the already-fetched items in the browser by name, case-insensitively
It re-renders the page on the server for every keystroke
quiz.feedback: The checkpoint explicitly requires a client-side filter with case-insensitive matching on the item name, with no new backend route.
